**Reduction.** Write p = x+y+z = 9, q = xy+yz+zx = 14, r = xyz.

Since (x²+y²)/(x+y) = (x+y) − 2xy/(x+y), and with t = 9−z we have xy = 14 − z(9−z), the term xy/(x+y) equals (t² − 9t + 14)/t = t − 9 + 14/t. Summing over the three pairs, with Σt = 18:

Expression = 18 − 2Σ xy/(x+y) = 36 − 28 Σ 1/(x+y).

**Computing Σ 1/(x+y).** The numerator is Σ(x+y)(x+z) = Σx² + 3q = (81 − 28) + 42 = 95. The denominator is (x+y)(y+z)(z+x) = pq − r = 126 − r. Hence

Σ 1/(x+y) = 95/(126 − r).

Minimizing the expression means maximizing r.

**Maximizing r.** x, y, z are the roots of f(t) = t³ − 9t² + 14t − r. Three positive real roots exist only for r up to the local maximum value of g(t) = t³ − 9t² + 14t. The critical points satisfy g′(t) = 3t² − 18t + 14 = 0, so t = 3 ± √39/3. The local maximum is at t₀ = 3 − √39/3 ≈ 0.918.

Using t₀² = 6t₀ − 14/3, we get g(t₀) = −(26/3)t₀ + 14 = (26√39 − 108)/9 ≈ 6.04.

At this r the roots are a double root t₀ and a third root 9 − 2t₀ ≈ 7.16. All are positive, so the maximum is attained (x = y = t₀, z = 9 − 2t₀).

**Value.** 126 − r = (1242 − 26√39)/9, so

Expression = 36 − 28·95·9/(1242 − 26√39) = 36 − 11970/(621 − 13√39).

Rationalizing: (621)² − 169·39 = 385641 − 6591 = 379050, and 11970/379050 = 3/95. So

11970/(621 − 13√39) = 3(621 + 13√39)/95 = (1863 + 39√39)/95.

Expression = (3420 − 1863 − 39√39)/95 = (1557 − 39√39)/95 ≈ 13.83.
